html:
Chan Chan was the capital of the Chimú kingdom on the north coast of Peru, near today's Trujillo, from about 850 until the Inca conquest around 1470. It was the largest adobe city in the Americas.

The Chimú ruled the coast for hundreds of kilometres, with canals bringing water from the Andes to the desert. Chan Chan covered about 20 square kilometres. At its centre were about ten walled compounds, each probably the palace and later the tomb of a king, decorated with friezes of fish, birds and waves. Tens of thousands of craftsmen and servants lived around them.

Around 1470 the armies of Topa Inca conquered the Chimú and took their craftsmen and goldsmiths to Cusco. Rain and looting have damaged the city, and it is on the list of World Heritage in Danger. It shows the coastal states of Peru that the Inca absorbed.
